title: Who Is This? People and Family
overview:
Name the people around you.
Say who they are to you.
Use he and she, not just the name.
Point and say: this is my sister.
functions: Name a person: man, woman, boy, girl
Say who a person is to you
Use he and she instead of a name
Point out a person near you and further away
Say how many people are in your family
learningPath: Patterns: this and that, he and she.
Say who is in your family.
Write three lines about a person.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 5. Today, people.
Until now you talked about yourself.
Now you talk about other people.
First, four words. Listen.
A man. A woman. A boy. A girl.
A man is big. A boy is young.
A woman is big. A girl is young.
Say them with me. Man. Woman. Boy. Girl.
Now your family.
Mother. Father. Sister. Brother.
Say them with me.
And two more. Wife. Husband.
Now, a small word that saves you.
You do not say the name every time.
For a man or a boy, say he.
For a woman or a girl, say she.
Listen. This is Ben. He is my brother.
This is Ana. She is my sister.
Say it with me. He is. She is.
Last, pointing.
Near you: this is my friend.
Far from you: that is my teacher.
This for near. That for far.
And the question: Who is this?
That is Unit 5. Go and talk about people.

grammar.title: He and she
grammar.explanation:
You do not say the name every time.
One small word does it.
He for a man or boy. She for a woman or girl.
grammar.rule:
Ben is my brother.  →  He is my brother.
Ana is my sister.   →  She is my sister.

man, boy, father, brother, husband, son  →  he
woman, girl, mother, sister, wife, daughter  →  she
grammar.workedExample:
You want to talk about Ana.
1. Say her name once: This is Ana.
2. Now do not say it again.
3. Ana is a woman, so use she.
4. Say: She is my sister.
5. Say: She is a nurse.
grammar.mistake:
Many languages use one word for both.
English has two, and they are not the same.
Using he for a woman is a real mistake here.
grammar.tip: He for a man. She for a woman.
grammar.practice:
He or she?
1. My father. ___
2. My sister. ___
3. The boy. ___
4. The woman. ___
5. My husband. ___
6. The girl. ___
grammar.answers:
1. He
2. She
3. He
4. She
5. He
6. She
Five or six right? Good. This one matters.

grammar.title: This and that
grammar.explanation:
Both point at a person or a thing.
The difference is how far away it is.
grammar.rule:
Near you:        This is my friend.
Further away:    That is my teacher.

This is my bag.   (in your hand)
That is my bag.   (across the room)
grammar.workedExample:
Your sister is beside you.
1. She is near, so use this.
2. Say: This is my sister.
3. Your teacher is across the room.
4. Far, so use that.
5. Say: That is my teacher.
grammar.mistake:
Do not use this for everything.
English speakers hear the difference.
Near is this. Far is that.
grammar.tip: This for near. That for far.
grammar.practice:
This or that?
1. The book in your hand. ___
2. The man at the door. ___
3. Your friend beside you. ___
4. A car in the street. ___
5. The pen you are holding. ___
grammar.answers:
1. This
2. That
3. This
4. That
5. This
Four or five right? You can point in English.

grammar.title: Who is this?
grammar.explanation:
One question for a person.
The answer gives a name, or says who they are.
grammar.rule:
Who is this?
This is Ana.
She is my sister.

Who is that man?
That is my father.

who = a person
what = a thing
grammar.workedExample:
A person points at your friend.
1. They ask: Who is this?
2. Give the name: This is Ana.
3. Then say who she is to you.
4. Say: She is my friend.
5. Two short lines is a good answer.
grammar.mistake:
Do not use what for a person.
No: What is this? (about a person)
Yes: Who is this?
grammar.tip: Who is for people. What is for things.
grammar.practice:
Who or what?
1. ___ is this? It is a pen.
2. ___ is this? This is my sister.
3. ___ is that man?
4. ___ is in your bag?
grammar.answers:
1. What
2. Who
3. Who
4. What
All four? You can ask about people and things.

grammar.title: One or more than one
grammar.explanation:
Most words add s for more than one.
Three words here do not.
Learn those three now.
grammar.rule:
one friend  →  two friends
one sister  →  two sisters

But:
one man    →  two men
one woman   →  two women
one child   →  two children

people is already more than one
grammar.workedExample:
You have two of them.
1. The word is sister.
2. Is it one of the three strange ones? No.
3. So add s.
4. Say: two sisters.
5. Now try man. It is strange: two men.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say two mans or two childs.
These three change their shape.
And never say one people. Say one person.
grammar.practice:
Write the plural.
1. one brother, two ___
2. one man, two ___
3. one child, two ___
4. one friend, two ___
5. one woman, two ___
grammar.answers:
1. brothers
2. men
3. children
4. friends
5. women
Four or five right? Good. The three strange ones are common words.

readings.title: My Family
readings.genre: One person talking about their family
readings.passage:
My family is not big.
My mother is a teacher.
She works at a school.
My father is a driver.
He works at night.
I have one sister.
She is a nurse.
I have no brothers.
We are four people.

readings.title: Who Is That?
readings.passage:
Who is that man?
That is my father.
And the woman?
She is my mother.
Who is the girl?
That is my sister.
She is eight.
And the baby?
That is my brother. He is one.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Man, woman, boy, girl
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. You will hear about a person.
Say: man, woman, boy or girl.
1. He is forty. He is my father.
2. She is eight. She is my sister.
3. She is thirty. She is my teacher.
4. He is ten. He is my son.
5. He is fifty. He is my uncle.
6. She is six. She is my daughter.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: 1 man, 2 girl, 3 woman, 4 boy, 5 man, 6 girl.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to describe a person. Say if it is a man or a woman.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Who is in your family?
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about your family.
1. My family is (big or small).
2. My mother is (something about her).
3. My father is (something about him).
4. We are (a number) people.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: did you use he and she, not just names?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor about two people in your family. Ask it a question back.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — This and that
speaking.instructions:
Point and say.
1. A thing in your hand: This is my ___.
2. A thing across the room: That is my ___.
3. A person beside you: This is my ___.
4. A person far away: That is my ___.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: this for near, that for far?
speaking.tutor: Point at two things for the tutor. Use this for one and that for the other.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Point and say.
One. A thing in your hand. This is my ...
Two. A thing across the room. That is my ...
Three. A person beside you. This is my ...
Four. A person far away. That is my ...
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: this for near, that for far?

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Who is this?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Who is this? B: This is my sister.
2. A: What is her name? B: Her name is Ana.
3. A: Who is that man? B: That is my father.
4. A: What does he do? B: He is a driver.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: he for the man, she for the sister?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor who three people are. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — He or she?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say he or she.
1. my father
2. my sister
3. the boy
4. the woman
5. my husband
6. the girl
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: he, she, he, she, he, she.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a person. Say he or she for each one.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The th in this and that
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
this ... that ... the ... they
Put your tongue between your teeth.
Let the air come out.
It is not d. It is not z.
Now say these lines.
This is my mother.
That is my brother.
Tap the mic. Say both lines.
Check: can you feel your tongue between your teeth?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say this and that. Say them back.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Three people
writing.prompt:
Write three lines.
One line for each person in your family.
Use he or she in each line.
writing.model:
My mother is a teacher. She works at a school.
My father is a driver. He works at night.
My sister is a nurse. She is twenty.
writing.criteria:
Three lines.
He or she in each one.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.support: Write one line only. Add the others later.
writing.extension: Add a line about a friend.

writing.title: Writing 2 — One person, three things
writing.prompt:
Choose one person you know.
Write three short lines about them.
Say who they are. Say what they do.
writing.model:
This is Ana.
She is my friend.
She is a nurse and she is kind.
writing.criteria:
Three lines about one person.
You name them in the first line.
You use he or she after that.
Each line has a full stop.
writing.extension: Now write three lines about a second person.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Which word?
activities.instructions:
Man, woman, boy or girl?
1. He is forty. ___
2. She is seven. ___
3. She is thirty. ___
4. He is nine. ___
5. He is sixty. ___
6. She is five. ___
activities.answers:
1. man
2. girl
3. woman
4. boy
5. man
6. girl
Five or six right: good.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 2 — One or more than one
activities.instructions:
Write the plural.
1. one sister, two ___
2. one man, two ___
3. one child, two ___
4. one friend, two ___
5. one woman, two ___
6. one brother, two ___
activities.answers:
1. sisters
2. men
3. children
4. friends
5. women
6. brothers
Five or six right: good.
The three strange ones are man, woman and child.

activities.title: Practice 3 — He or she?
activities.instructions:
Write he or she.
1. My father is here. ___ is a driver.
2. My sister is here. ___ is a nurse.
3. The boy is ten. ___ is my son.
4. The woman is my teacher. ___ is kind.
5. My husband works. ___ works at night.
6. The girl is eight. ___ is my daughter.
activities.answers:
1. He
2. She
3. He
4. She
5. He
6. She
Five or six right: good. This is a mistake worth fixing.

activities.title: Practice 4 — This or that?
activities.instructions:
Write this or that.
1. A pen in your hand. ___
2. A car in the street. ___
3. Your friend beside you. ___
4. A man at the far door. ___
5. The book you are holding. ___
activities.answers:
1. this
2. that
3. this
4. that
5. this
Four or five right: good.
activities.solo: Point at each one as you answer.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Who or what?
activities.instructions:
Write who or what.
1. ___ is this? It is a bag.
2. ___ is this? This is my brother.
3. ___ is that woman?
4. ___ is in the box?
5. ___ is your teacher?
6. ___ is your name?
activities.answers:
1. What
2. Who
3. Who
4. What
5. Who
6. What
Five or six right: good. Who is for people only.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read and answer
activities.instructions:
Read My Family again. Answer these.
1. How many people?
2. What does the mother do?
3. When does the father work?
4. Is there a brother?
5. What does the sister do?
activities.answers:
1. Four
2. She is a teacher
3. At night
4. No
5. She is a nurse
Four or five right: you can read a short text about people.
activities.solo: Read the text, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: A grown-up female person is a ___.
quizzes.why: A girl is young. A woman is grown up.

quizzes.q: A young male person is a ___.
quizzes.why: A boy is young. A man is grown up.

quizzes.q: More than one child is two ___.
quizzes.why: Child is one of three words that change shape.

quizzes.q: My father is here. ___ is a driver.
quizzes.why: Father is a man, so he.

quizzes.q: My sister is here. ___ is a nurse.
quizzes.why: Sister is a woman, so she.

quizzes.q: Which word goes with a woman?
quizzes.why: She is for a woman or a girl. He is for a man or a boy.

quizzes.q: A pen is in your hand. You say: ___ is my pen.
quizzes.why: This is for near. That is for far.

quizzes.q: A car is across the street. You say: ___ is my car.
quizzes.why: That is for something further away.

quizzes.q: ___ is this? This is my brother.
quizzes.why: Who asks about a person. What asks about a thing.

quizzes.q: Someone asks: Who is that? What do they want to know?
quizzes.why: Who always asks about a person.

quizzes.q: More than one man is two ___.
quizzes.why: Man, woman and child all change shape.
People is already more than one. You never say peoples here.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: He and she is a real mistake, not a small one
teacherNotes.note: Many languages use one pronoun for both, so a learner may call their mother he for months without noticing. English listeners hear it immediately and it can sound careless when it is nothing of the kind. Correct it every time, kindly, and say why.

Asking an adult learner about their family is not a neutral warm-up. Some are here without the people they are naming. Let the learner choose who to talk about, accept a short answer, and never press for the ones they leave out.

teacherNotes.type: The first unit about somebody else
teacherNotes.note: Units 1 to 4 were all about the learner. This is the first time they describe another person, which is what he and she exist for. If a learner keeps repeating the name, that is the thing to work on.
Man, woman and child. They are irregular and they are also among the most used nouns in the language, so they have to be learned here rather than left for later.

I can say who is in my family.
I can use he and she.

I can ask who a person is.

assignment.title: The people in my life
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say four lines about your family.
Use he and she, not only names.
2. Write three lines about one person you know.
Say who they are and what they do.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
